name: oracle_surplus_throughput
patch_description:
Replace fixed quiet-window batches with inventory-sensitive sizing. From turn 256, demanded goods can sell 3–6 additional units when forecast supply is weak and the current quote is at least the base price. Non-demanded goods receive a smaller 3–4-unit allowance only with a particularly quiet forecast. Sizing uses inventory remaining after feed reserves and existing orders; missing forecasts never qualify as evidence of quiet conditions. MELON retains its conservative treatment.

Also reuse the less restrictive WOOL front-run and surplus-FERTILIZER settings present in the stronger supplied candidates. These should reduce inventory waiting for prices that may not recover, while retaining one fertilizer and leaving feed protection, opening expenditure, worker routes, and emergency shed-pressure handling unchanged. The prior results support testing these settings together, but do not isolate their individual effects.

Finally, make sell consolidation tuple-safe so an existing tuple order cannot silently revert the entire turn to the backbone. The expected benefit is faster surplus conversion with bounded batch increases, rather than speculative buying or forecast-dependent production changes.
